topics.label: Lecture Introduction
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer welcomes the students and outlines the focus of the session on the initiation and resolution of inflammation.

topics.label: Foundations of Innate Recognition: PAMPs, DAMPs, and PRRs
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the foundational principles by which the innate immune system senses pathogens and tissue damage through conserved molecular patterns and spatially positioned receptors.

topics.label: Pattern Recognition Receptor Families and Signaling Cascades
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the major families of pattern recognition receptors, their intracellular signaling pathways, and the assembly of the inflammatory inflammasome complex.

topics.label: Cellular Dynamics and Systemic Manifestations of Inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the cellular responses triggered during an active inflammatory response, including leukocyte trafficking, lymphatic drainage, and severe systemic outcomes like septic shock.

topics.label: Resolution of Inflammation, Tissue Repair, and Chronic Pathology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how inflammatory responses are terminated and repaired, alongside the circumstances leading to persistent chronic inflammation and granuloma formation.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session and previews the upcoming lecture topic.
